extraction.reason: Not recorded when the page was cached, and not recovered since. What the .txt shows is a tag-stripping of the .html rather than a browser rendering: it keeps the site navigation chrome, decodes entities, holds each paragraph on one line, and carries artefacts only a regex stripper leaves - a bare `--->` where a comment opened with a `>` inside it, and a fragment of a meta attribute ending `">`. Two candidates were run on 2026-09-09 and NEITHER reproduces extractedTextSha256: a regex stripper (tags to newlines, entities decoded, blank lines dropped) and Chromium's document.body.innerText through Playwright. This is not cosmetic: content/levels/halifax.json cites this digest as the sourceHash of its territory statement, so a shipped claim is pinned to bytes that only a machine already holding the file can produce. Someone who fetched the page and matched its sha256 still cannot check the quote.

knownStaleness.topic: A maintained page describing live negotiations
knownStaleness.problem: The two sections about what is happening TODAY - the Marshall negotiations in the Maritimes and Gaspé, and what becomes of the treaties once a long-term agreement is signed - describe a process that is still running and can be overtaken by an agreement without the page being rewritten. The historical section this cache is cited for, that the Peace and Friendship Treaties did not involve surrendering rights to the land, is a statement about eighteenth-century documents and does not expire.

grainNote: One web page, four headings, no pagination, so `pages` is absent and a chapter carries a title alone. The staleness flag is scoped to the two present-tense sections rather than to the whole page, which is the discrimination `discover-canada.json`'s own grainNote asks for: the historical section a territory statement cites is not made volatile by negotiations moving.
